_: AES-256-GCM known-answer vectors, from the NIST-referenced GCM specification test-case set
(McGrew & Viega, 'The Galois/Counter Mode of Operation', cases 13–16 — the AES-256 block).
These drive `gcmEncrypt`/`gcmDecrypt` in src/crypto/envelope.ts, which is why those two are
exported at all: a vector pins the IV and a raw AAD, so it cannot be pushed through `seal()`,
which generates its own IV and builds the AAD from the canonical `{ v, purpose, id }` JSON.
Testing them through `crypto.subtle` directly would only prove the platform works.
`ct` is the ciphertext with the 16-byte tag already appended, which is how WebCrypto returns it
and how the wire format stores it. All byte fields are hex.
128-bit keys, 64-bit tags, and non-96-bit IVs are absent on purpose: we use exactly one
parameter set (AES-256, 96-bit IV, 128-bit tag) and a vector for anything else would be testing
a configuration that must never appear.

aes256.name: Case 13 — empty plaintext, empty AAD, zero key and IV
Case 14 — one zero block, empty AAD
Case 16 — truncated plaintext with a 20-byte AAD

_wireFormat: A pinned sealed blob in VaultaMark's own envelope format, so a change to the framing — the
version byte, the field order, the AAD's canonical JSON — fails a test instead of silently
making every existing vault unreadable. `open()` must return `plaintextUtf8` for these bytes.
Regenerating this because it stopped matching is exactly the wrong response: it is a format
change, and a format change needs a SCHEMA_VERSION bump and a migration.

wireFormat.plaintextUtf8: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
